[DAY3 21:33:00 - DAY3 22:33:00]
I began the cake preparation by carefully selecting suitable layers from a large stack, with Lucia assisting by holding the pieces while I measured and cut them to the desired thickness and dimensions. We discussed appropriate layer thicknesses, with Lucia advising against cuts that were too thin to maintain structural integrity. Tasha joined the process by weighing ingredients and directing the addition of sugar and cream. Based on their feedback about moisture and texture, I adjusted cutting tools and techniques to refine the cake’s layered structure progressively. This collaborative effort resulted in four precisely cut layers, which I set aside after receiving positive feedback from Alice and others, marking a successful completion of the cake layer preparation phase.

Transitioning to fruit preparation, I washed a knife and peeled, sliced, and removed mango flesh into small pieces following Tasha’s instructions, who also demonstrated proper hand and fruit washing methods. I assisted by further cutting the mango into smaller segments and placing them on a plate. Meanwhile, Lucia and Tasha prepared strawberries and managed utensils. We coordinated tasks efficiently, noting the absence of some tools such as scissors and sharing responsibilities to maintain workflow. Upon completing the fruit preparation, I washed my hands, discarded peels, and briefly discussed fruit weights and seasoning adjustments with Shure before the group moved on to the next stage.

Next, I assisted Tasha in decorating the cake by squeezing cream from a piping bag onto the cake layers, practicing technique under her guidance. While Shure sampled barbecue food nearby, I continued the decoration by balancing cream application and smoothing the surface with a scraper, following Lucia’s directions. We discussed hygiene practices and fruit arrangement methods during this phase while sharing food, maintaining a balance between decoration and social interaction. I whipped cream carefully to build layers and edges, incorporating input from Tasha and Lucia, who added toppings to complete the cake’s surface. This stage concluded the initial cream layering and decoration.

In parallel with the decoration, I managed seating arrangements by moving a stool and coordinating with the group regarding available seats. I engaged in discussions with Tasha and Lucia about the cake’s size and stability, encouraging the addition of cream layers despite concerns about the cake potentially toppling due to its height. Our interactions included lighthearted remarks about the process while maintaining an organized and collaborative environment focused on refining the cake’s appearance and texture. This coordination ensured comfort and effective teamwork during the ongoing decoration.

I executed the final cream spreading and smoothing steps by following Tasha’s demonstrations and Lucia’s advice to evenly coat the cake edges and top. Using a scraper, I flattened the cream while spinning the cake plate to blend surfaces seamlessly. The team compared the cake to a beginner’s attempt but acknowledged its improved quality, noting progress made during the session. Upon completing the frosting, I confirmed the cake was nearly finished as we prepared to transition to the next activity, marking the conclusion of the cake decoration phase with shared satisfaction and readiness to proceed.

Continuing the cream application, I evenly spread cream on the cake while multitasking by smoothing and pressing the frosting with a scraper and spinning the cake plate to achieve a consistent surface. Lucia and Tasha observed and provided comments on the cake’s appearance and technique, including remarks about water depth and playful comparisons to other cakes. I inspected my work, acknowledged limitations of the materials, and discussed strategies focusing on color and surface finishing rather than exterior painting. Throughout this phase, I encouraged tasting barbecue meat alongside the cake work, balancing task execution with social interaction. This collaborative effort prioritized cake restoration and efficient use of materials.

I supervised the cake decoration while interacting with Katrina, Tasha, Lucia, and Shure. Katrina prepared to photograph the cake and received a thumbs-up from me as a signal of readiness. Tasha applied powder to the cake while Katrina sampled meat. I referred to this step as “the finishing touch” and discussed its significance with Lucia. Shure commented on the dish’s oil content, noting it was insufficient. I held the plate during Tasha’s fruit and strawberry decoration, which Lucia praised. As Tasha completed the setup, she sprinkled powder with a spatula while Lucia and Shure took photographs. I reapplied cream after shaking and scraping, inspected the cake’s back side, and confirmed its appearance was satisfactory. Tasha then poured powder into an hourglass and evenly sprinkled it during Katrina’s photography. The group celebrated the completed decoration, with Shure noting the cake’s size and offering to introduce its creator, concluding the collaborative decoration and photography session.

I prepared to cut strawberries while Tasha arranged them and explained cutting methods. Shure encouraged me to perform the “historic cut,” and I requested guidance. Tasha allowed a free cutting style, though Shure noted that slicing five pieces would be challenging. Following a lighthearted discussion that included AI advice, I began cutting with support and caution from Lucia and others. During cutting, a strawberry fell, prompting laughter and calls for repair. I set aside the fallen pieces for patching and adjusted cuts based on group suggestions. Tasha noted the changing appearance of the strawberry pieces, and I continued refining them, completing the cutting task with group interaction and management of mishaps.

I selected suitable cake pieces for removal using a shovel, noting that few ideal parts remained. Observing others, I exchanged brief comments with Lucia about the cake’s appearance. I then transferred strawberries to a new position on the cake, scraped the surface to even it, and placed a piece on a plate. Lucia identified the item as a crepe, and Shure expressed confidence in the completion of the cake assembly. Despite the instability of the strawberry placement, I continued adjustments, noting the result looked “a bit ugly,” while Tasha described it as fancy. This finalized the assembly and presentation of the cake with strawberries, concluding the group’s task on cake assembly.

I scooped a cake piece, assessed its acceptability, and transferred it onto a plate with Tasha’s assistance. Pressing the cake into shape, I prepared for tiramisu as directed by Lucia. Continuing, I cut and arranged additional cake pieces, added strawberries, and used a scraper to even the portions. Lucia complimented the appearance, while Tasha remarked on the task’s difficulty. After decorating, I mixed the cake evenly and positioned items on plates, while Lucia rinsed dishes. I inquired about proper cake cutting methods from Tasha and then moved to the kitchen, where I accidentally spilled a plate but secured the cake away from exposure. This completed the cake and tiramisu preparation and arrangement.

I engaged with Lucia and Tasha in a discussion about the cake’s transformation from a traditional to a contemporary style while demonstrating whipped cream application. After washing my hands, I confirmed with Tasha and Alice that there were sufficient plates for serving. Later, I checked the cake in the oven and, following Lucia’s suggestion, added cream to enhance it. I conversed lightly with Tasha about her brother and coordinated with Lucia on plate placement, monitoring progress. Upon the arrival of Katrina and Tasha, I consoled Shure and observed Alice’s baking activity. Shure advised on grilling technique and charcoal arrangement, which I acknowledged. I facilitated communication among the group and supported tasks while Katrina observed silently.

Entering the hall with Tasha and Lucia, I invited them to share the pre-dinner dessert, sampling cake and discussing its texture and preparation. Tasha explained the cake base’s design, and I reflected on my role in mixing the ingredients. We shared bites and commented on the layers and cream, maintaining casual culinary dialogue. Continuing, I offered to grill meat while peeling fruit and cutting pieces. Tasha and Lucia ate with me, expressing enjoyment. This relaxed moment combined food sharing with meal planning. Toward the end, Tasha and Lucia prepared to leave while I remained, concluding the dessert session.

After eating cake pieces, I observed Lucia and Tasha preparing whipped cream, briefly discussing cream sweetness and quantity. Upon finishing, I cleaned my plate and announced readiness to go outside to fetch meat as prompted by Lucia. Outside, I coordinated with Alice, Shure, and Katrina about food selection and serving, volunteering to retrieve meat for the group. Subsequently, I rinsed cake plates with Lucia, identified skewers for cleaning, confirmed oven contents, and completed kitchen cleanup, preparing the space for the next phase.

Carrying a plate of grilled meat, I transitioned from kitchen cleanup to serving outdoors, exchanging remarks with Lucia and Tasha about desserts. During group food preparation, I managed utensils by washing and distributing chopsticks, confirmed lighting arrangements with Katrina, and acknowledged Shure’s input on AI communication datasets. While others ate, I maintained kitchen tasks and ensured meal setup, reflecting my central facilitation role in the event.

Checking for chopsticks, I found none in the cabinet but located a pair elsewhere, confirming sufficiency with Lucia. I washed used chopsticks as advised, coordinated with Tasha’s serving plans, and then ate meat using the chopsticks, responding affirmatively to Shure’s inquiry about hunger. Afterward, I observed Lucia whipping cream and Tasha bringing the cake, briefly engaging before talking with Alice outside about pot readiness. Alice fed me a bite, which I confirmed as delicious. During this time, Katrina commented on emotional difficulty related to video content, and I noticed Lucia requesting assistance with a piping bag, indicating ongoing preparation.

I began initial preparation by cleaning a kitchen knife and cutting strawberries following Lucia’s instructions. Tasha brought strawberries, which I cut open to facilitate her separation, while Lucia washed strawberries and a plate. I handled cream mixing using a stirring stick and scraper, then assisted Tasha by filling a piping bag using a shovel. During this process, Tasha and I addressed connection issues with a device, resolving them by plugging in a cable. I managed timing with software while Lucia monitored progress. After completion, we reviewed the results, confirming with Tasha and noting Lucia’s observation about image reversal. Though some cream pieces fell causing minor mess, we assessed our baking skills humorously, concluding minimal but present talent, thus completing the preparation stage.

[DAY3 21:54:00 - DAY3 21:57:00]
I assist Tasha by reaching out to help squeeze cream and observe as she demonstrates squeezing out a circle, then teaches me the technique. She then hands me the piping bag to try, and I begin squeezing cream while Tasha and Shure inspect the work. Shure enters holding barbecue, which leads to a brief discussion and tasting; I continue squeezing cream as Shure samples and eventually takes the plate away. This segment concludes with me filling the last portion of cream and watching Lucia smooth the surface with a scraper while Tasha arranges fruit on top.

Next, I engage in conversation with Lucia and Tasha about hygiene and fruit arrangement, asking Lucia how she manages scraping cream and receiving advice on technique. We discuss cleanliness levels humorously, reflecting on the kitchen environment and concluding that hygiene standards vary but are generally overlooked. During this, Shure brings me a skewer of grilled meat, which I eat while chatting with the group. Shure confirms no issues with the food and offers another skewer, while I continue decorating my cake by squeezing more cream.

In the final stage, I whip cream in a circular motion, balancing support with one hand and squeezing with the other, following Tasha and Lucia’s advice to smooth the top layer and build the cream higher around the edges. They suggest using excess cream for cupcakes if needed. As I work, Tasha sprinkles toppings on the cake, assisted by Lucia, while I keep squeezing the piping bag. We all watch the progress and share light remarks about the food, concluding the session with laughter and mutual appreciation of the cake decoration process.

[DAY3 21:57:00 - DAY3 22:00:00]
I moved a stool from the computer room to the middle seat by first freeing it when it got stuck, then carrying and setting it down. I instructed others to get stools from Duya, but Lucia declined, mentioning she had enough in her room, leading to a brief exchange about hoarding stools. After settling, I sat down and resumed whipping cream, with Lucia assisting while Tasha and I observed.

We collaboratively discussed cake preparation, including piping and size, while watching Lucia whip and smooth the cream. Tasha took charge of arranging fruit on the cake layers, and I provided guidance, encouraging her to add more cream layers. We shared light conversation about the cake’s shape and structure, noting it was tall and might topple easily when cut, but agreed to proceed regardless.

As we worked, I squeezed cream to create defining layers, joking about the cake resembling a burger and expressing amusement at the process. I continued to whip and sort the cream carefully, with Lucia and Tasha advising caution to avoid mishaps. Our teamwork focused on perfecting the cream layers and cake assembly, maintaining an organized and collaborative approach throughout.
